POPs are bioaccumulated in adipose tissue and that POPs are associated with the promotion of breast cancer.
POPs, obesity, and diabetes are linked and that obesity may be an intermediate factor that links POPs and breast cancer.
POPs, which are endocrine-disrupting compounds that bioaccumulate in fat tissue and are correlated with obesity, can also influence breast cancer cell growth and survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mechanistic understanding of the relationship between obesity, POPs and breast cancer.
understanding the mechanisms by which POPs influence obesity, inflammation, and breast cancer development and progression.
the potential role of POPs in the development of obesity, diabetes, and cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity is a risk factor for breast cancer, and POPs may play a role in promoting obesity and/or breast cancer development.
POPs are a potential risk factor for obesity and breast cancer.
POPs and obesity may be a contributing factor for the promotion of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POPs are endocrine disruptors and can cause obesity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
POPs are a potential mechanism by which obesity influences the development and progression of breast cancer.
POPs are a major environmental factor that can contribute to obesity and, in turn, breast cancer development and progression.
